classification.difficultyReason: Every part is a standard z-score and table routine with the method signposted. The hardest part is a. It is a between-probability with z = -1 and 1.14, where the student must use symmetry for the negative z (1 - P(Z ≤ 1)) and subtract table values. Parts b to d are single-tail or between lookups with rounded z. Part e scales a probability by 1000. This is slightly above p48-q8, which has only positive z-scores and a count, and below p56-q21, which adds contextual reasoning about 'early' and 'late'. There is no interpretation or judgement task.

content.prompt: The heights of 1000 Year 12 males are found to be approximately normally distributed with a mean of 168 cm and standard deviation of 9 cm. Use the standard normal distribution table. Round calculated z-scores to 2 decimal places and give probabilities to 4 decimal places.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The time taken by a bus to travel from Penrith to Parramatta is normally distributed with a mean of 52 minutes and a standard deviation of 7 minutes. What is the probability that a randomly chosen trip takes between 45 and 60 minutes? Use the standard normal table, rounding z-scores to 2 decimal places. Give the probability to 4 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Let $X$ be the trip time in minutes.
$$\begin{align*}z_1&=\frac{45-52}{7}=-1\\z_2&=\frac{60-52}{7}=\frac87\approx1.14\end{align*}$$
By symmetry and the standard normal table,
$$\begin{align*}P(45<X<60)&\approx P(-1<Z<1.14)\\&=P(Z\le1.14)-P(Z\le-1)\\&=P(Z\le1.14)-\left(1-P(Z\le1)\right)\\&\approx0.8729-(1-0.8413)\\&\approx0.7142\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: How many Year 12 males in the sample are expected to have a height between 170 cm and 175 cm?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Expected number}&=np\\\text{Expected number}&\approx1000\times0.1952\\\text{Expected number}&=195.2\\\text{Expected number}&\approx195\end{aligned}$$
Approximately 195 Year 12 males.
